decisions.quote: Comparison of these results with those of Hofmann and Fisher's (2012) study on thematic self-control revealed that previous guilt had beneficial indirect pathways on subsequent self-control processes (goal importance, conflict, and resistance) to inhibit desire-related behavior. However, the latter reported that guilt for self-control failures had detrimental residual effects on subsequent behavioral inhibition, whereas the former did not demonstrate such a negative effect. Furthermore, although Hofmann and Fisher (2012) found that previous pride had beneficial indirect pathways on subsequent self-control processes, this study found no positive impact of pride on self-control processes.
decisions.reason: The shipped quote from the abstract ('In addition to replicating Hofmann and Fisher's results (2012), we also examined...') describes the study's aim to conduct a replication alongside additional analyses (paralleled in the Introduction, Results, and Discussion), not an overall outcome verdict. In the Results and Discussion, the author explicitly compares the findings against Hofmann and Fisher (2012) and reports mixed results: the beneficial indirect effect of guilt on subsequent self-control processes replicated, whereas the detrimental direct effect of guilt on behavioral inhibition and the beneficial indirect effects of pride on self-control processes did not replicate.
